parsedVerdict.reasoning: TaskController is an Express HTTP adapter in the infrastructure layer. It wires routes, turns request bodies, path parameters and query strings into application inputs, calls the application use cases, and maps errors to HTTP status codes. These are all transport and adapter jobs, which belong in infrastructure. The checks in requiredString, object, optionalString and pathParam only confirm that the request is well-formed (right shape, strings present). They are not business rules. Checking task status is handed off to the domain's isTaskStatus, so the controller does not hold domain logic itself. Business work (creating users, projects and tasks, listing tasks, marking a task done) is done by the use cases. One small issue: the controller throws DomainError for request-shape problems. That borrows a domain error type for transport validation. It does not move a business rule into this file, so it is not a layer-role violation.
